reference: OpenSSH ssh-keygen -F and -R for known_hosts filtering/removal; documented Bash ssh help/verify contracts for loadable-only behavior. The fixed Ed25519 public key is the RFC 8032 test vector encoded as an SSH public-key blob. The hashed-host fixture uses OpenSSH's documented HMAC-SHA1 known_hosts format with a fixed 20-byte salt, independently calculated.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata without invoking transport operations
Documented known-hosts add and verify contracts using relative fixture files
OpenSSH known_hosts filtering for plain, hashed, comma-separated alias, and absent entries
OpenSSH known_hosts removal and resulting file state
exclusions: No SSH network activity, authentication, external host, installed credentials, PTY, or system service is used.
SSH transport, keyscan, forwarding, multiplexing, SFTP, and interactive shell behavior remain deferred pending an explicitly disposable isolated peer and suitable fixture drivers.

This audit covers ordinary plain/hashed host fields and comma-separated literal aliases in private files. Marker records, wildcard/negated patterns, symlink/concurrent update behavior and environmental I/O failures are not qualified.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata identifies ssh as a loadable builtin without running an ssh operation.
Bash help exposes the documented client verbs and known-hosts interface; the script emits a stable marker after checking those help entries.
cases.script:
doc=$(help ssh)
[[ $doc == *"connect HOST"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"exec HANDLE CMD"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"known-hosts verify HOST"* ]]
printf 'ssh help metadata ok\n'

cases.purpose: The documented add operation appends a host/key record to the explicitly configured relative known_hosts fixture; stdout reads back the resulting content.
cases.script:
export BASHSSH_KNOWN_HOSTS=known_hosts
key='ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAINdamAGCsQq31Uv+08lkBzoO4XLz2qYjJa8CGmj3B1Ea'
printf 'retained.fixture.test %s\n' "$key" > known_hosts
ssh known-hosts add added.fixture.test "$key"
while IFS= read -r line; do printf '%s\n' "$line"; done < known_hosts

cases.purpose: The documented verifier distinguishes a matching key, a recorded key mismatch, and an unknown host with return codes 0, 1, and 2.
cases.script:
export BASHSSH_KNOWN_HOSTS=known_hosts
key='ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAINdamAGCsQq31Uv+08lkBzoO4XLz2qYjJa8CGmj3B1Ea'
printf 'fixture.test %s\n' "$key" > known_hosts
record_status() {
  local actual
  if ssh known-hosts verify "$1" "$2"; then actual=0; else actual=$?; fi
  printf '%s\n' "$actual"
}
record_status fixture.test "$key"
record_status fixture.test wrong-key
record_status unknown.fixture.test "$key"

cases.purpose: A filtered lookup returns the matching plain known_hosts record byte-for-byte, using ssh-keygen -F as the OpenSSH oracle.
cases.script:
export BASHSSH_KNOWN_HOSTS=known_hosts
key='ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAINdamAGCsQq31Uv+08lkBzoO4XLz2qYjJa8CGmj3B1Ea'
printf '# fixture comment\n\nother.fixture.test %s\nplain.fixture.test %s\n' "$key" "$key" > known_hosts
if [[ $(type -t ssh) == builtin ]]; then
  ssh known-hosts list plain.fixture.test
else
  ssh-keygen -q -F plain.fixture.test -f known_hosts
fi

cases.purpose: A fixed OpenSSH HMAC-SHA1 hashed host record is found and then removed; status, stdout, stderr policy, and resulting fixture tree are compared with ssh-keygen -F/-R.
cases.script:
export BASHSSH_KNOWN_HOSTS=known_hosts
key='ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAINdamAGCsQq31Uv+08lkBzoO4XLz2qYjJa8CGmj3B1Ea'
printf '# retain this comment\n|1|AAECAwQFBgcICQoLDA0ODxAREhM=|n9LVS+f9nF1+/FfRFwRpux5+lGs= %s\nother.fixture.test %s\n' "$key" "$key" > known_hosts
if [[ $(type -t ssh) == builtin ]]; then
  ssh known-hosts list hash.fixture.test
  ssh known-hosts remove hash.fixture.test
else
  ssh-keygen -q -F hash.fixture.test -f known_hosts
  ssh-keygen -R hash.fixture.test -f known_hosts
fi

cases.purpose: Removing one plain host leaves unrelated records, comments, and blank lines in the fixture file as OpenSSH ssh-keygen -R does.

printf '# preserved comment\n\nremove.fixture.test %s\nkeep.fixture.test %s\n' "$key" "$key" > known_hosts
if [[ $(type -t ssh) == builtin ]]; then

else
  ssh-keygen -R remove.fixture.test -f known_hosts
fi

cases.purpose: Find aliases case-insensitively, preserving the original whitespace and key record bytes printed by the independent oracle.
cases.script:
export BASHSSH_KNOWN_HOSTS=known_hosts
key='ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAINdamAGCsQq31Uv+08lkBzoO4XLz2qYjJa8CGmj3B1Ea'
printf ' \tPrimary.fixture.test,Alias.fixture.test %s\n' "$key" > known_hosts
if [[ $(type -t ssh) == builtin ]]; then
  ssh known-hosts list ALIAS.fixture.test
else
  ssh-keygen -q -F ALIAS.fixture.test -f known_hosts
fi

cases.purpose: Remove all alias-bearing records while preserving unrelated lines and the original 0600 file mode. Compare the complete .old backup and an existing old-backup replacement.
cases.script:
export BASHSSH_KNOWN_HOSTS=known_hosts
key='ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAINdamAGCsQq31Uv+08lkBzoO4XLz2qYjJa8CGmj3B1Ea'
printf 'old backup\n' > known_hosts.old
printf '# fixture\nprimary.fixture.test,alias.fixture.test %s\nkeep.fixture.test %s\nalias.fixture.test %s\n' "$key" "$key" "$key" > known_hosts
chmod 600 known_hosts
if [[ $(type -t ssh) == builtin ]]; then
  ssh known-hosts remove alias.fixture.test
else
  ssh-keygen -R alias.fixture.test -f known_hosts
fi
